caption:
An AI "solved" a $1M problem.
Lean-verified, not peer-reviewed. OpenAI announcement, 8 Sept 2026; Nature news d41586-026-02842-5; Fields Medallists' statement, 11 Sept 2026.

OpenAI announced on 8 Sept 2026 a multi-agent proof that the forced 3D Navier-Stokes equations can blow up in finite time (Clay cases C and D, not the unforced A and B). By OpenAI's own account: about 10,000 agents, about 88 hours, Lean formalisation in 17 hours. It says it will not claim the prize. On 11 Sept, 25 Fields Medallists at launch published 'A Severe Misalignment of AI in Mathematics', saying AI companies' goals and mathematicians' goals are 'severely misaligned'. Lean-verified but not peer-reviewed. A priority dispute has been reported. Coverage: Nature news, Quanta, 2026. Declaration: https://terrytao.wordpress.com/2026/09/11/a-severe-misalignment-of-ai-in-mathematics/ We will follow it.

#ai #mathematics #science #openai
voiceover_script: An AI, quote, solved, unquote, a million dollar maths problem. That is the headline. Here is the contested version. OpenAI says its agents proved that a forced Navier-Stokes fluid can blow up. On September eighth, it announced that around ten thousand agents, running for about eighty eight hours, produced that proof, with a further seventeen hours to formalise it in Lean. Forced versus unforced matters here, and OpenAI itself says it will not claim the prize. Three days later, twenty five Fields Medallists published a statement titled A Severe Misalignment of AI in Mathematics. The work is not peer-reviewed, and a priority dispute has been reported. Big claim, big pushback.
